sentences.text: Every entry on a cairn site becomes HTML through the adapter's `rendering.render`, and the edit page's preview and every public page call that same function.
The preview calls it in the editor's browser and the public entry route calls it from a server `load`, so a component's code runs in both places.
A custom public component is a container directive in the markdown that the site's `build` function turns into markup.
One registry of components feeds the render pipeline through `createRenderer` and the editor's picker through the admin page.
A new custom public component sits beside the ones a site already declares, such as the nine that a scaffolded site ships in `markdown-components.ts` under `src/theme/`.
Writing one means declaring it, writing its `build` function, shaping its entry in the picker, registering it, and checking that the preview and the published page render it alike.
One developer arrives wanting authors to insert a structured block, with fields and regions to fill, from the editor's picker and to see it in the site's markup.
Another is adding an island.
An island starts as a component declared with `hydrate`, so that developer writes the declaration here first.
For a component that misbehaves, [Diagnose a failed check](#diagnose-a-failed-check) maps each symptom to its cause, from a directive printed as literal text to a preview that refuses to render.
The running example is an `event` component with a date, a place, a details body, and an agenda list.
The page assumes you know TypeScript and can build a hast element with hastscript's `h()`.
It also assumes an adapter file whose render function is built with `createRenderer`: a scaffolded site ships one, and the add-cairn tutorial writes one by hand.
This page leaves the following topics to the pages that cover them:
Building the render function, in [Add cairn to a SvelteKit app](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md) and the [`createRenderer`](../reference/core.md#createrenderer) entry.
Adding a remark plugin and setting the renderer options, in the [`createRenderer`](../reference/core.md#createrenderer) entry.
A scaffolded site already passes the smartypants plugin to its one `createRenderer` call.
The classes the built-in render steps emit for code, tables, and figures, in [Emitted classes](../reference/render.md#emitted-classes).
What the sanitize floor and the sink guard protect, in [Render safety](security-model.md#render-safety).
Hydrating a component in the browser, in [Add an island](add-an-island.md).
Styling the rendered output, in [Style rendered markdown](theme-your-public-site.md#style-rendered-markdown).
Fragments and `::include`, in [Reuse content across entries](reuse-content-across-entries.md).
The media resolver and missing assets, in [Configure media](configure-media.md).
Before you write a component, make sure your site has the following:
An adapter file whose `rendering.render` calls a renderer built with `createRenderer`.
The adapter is `src/theme/cairn.config.ts` on a scaffolded site and `src/lib/cairn.config.ts` on the add-cairn tutorial's site.

The tutorial writes its adapter in [Write the site config and a minimal adapter](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#write-the-site-config-and-a-minimal-adapter), and the [`createRenderer`](../reference/core.md#createrenderer) entry documents the renderer.
The `hastscript` package, to build the markup a component returns.
For its `h()` API, see [hastscript](https://github.com/syntax-tree/hastscript).
The scaffold lists it as a dependency.
On a hand-built site, install it with the following command:
A module that holds the components.
A scaffolded site keeps them in `markdown-components.ts` under `src/theme/`, and the adapter builds its registry from that module's `components` list.
`defineComponent` declares one container directive.
It requires a `name`, a `label`, a `description`, and a `build` function.
Its optional members include `attributes`, `slots`, `behavior`, and `hydrate`.
An author always writes a component as a container directive, opening it with `:::name[Title]{attrs}` and closing it with `:::`.
A leaf `::name` or text `:name` form renders as its literal source text.
The names `figure` and `include` belong to the engine's render steps, and a component can't take either.
To declare the component, follow these steps:
In `markdown-components.ts`, import `defineComponent` and `fields` from the engine, and `h` from `hastscript`.
In the same file, export a `defineComponent` call with the `name`, `label`, and `description`.
In the call, add an `attributes` object that maps each attribute name to one `fields.*` descriptor.
In the call, add a `build` stub that returns an empty element.
On a hand-built site, the file can be any module that the adapter imports.
The following declaration gives `event` a required `date` attribute, an optional `place` attribute, and a `build` stub that [Write the build function](#write-the-build-function) completes:
An attribute takes a field type that serializes to one attribute string.
The ten such types are `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `select`, `url`, `email`, `date`, `datetime`, `boolean`, and `icon`.
Any other type, such as `multiselect` or `image`, throws when the module loads.
The message includes `a directive attribute must be a single-value scalar`.
Before the insert form inserts a component, it validates the attributes with the same fieldset validator that a concept's fields use.
A cross-field rule goes in the component's `behavior` member, keyed by attribute name.
The render validates no attribute value, and a hand-typed `date` of `banana` still reaches `build` as that string.
A `build` has to handle a value the form would refuse.
`defaultIconByRole` maps a value of the directive's `role` attribute to a glyph key, and it overrides the engine's default glyph for each role it names.
The [`defineComponent`](../reference/core.md#definecomponent) entry lists every member.
The [Fields](../reference/core.md#fields) table states what each field type renders in the form.
Setting `hydrate` makes the component an island, and [Add an island](add-an-island.md) covers the rest.
A slot's name sets its place in the directive.
A slot named `title` is the bracketed label, a slot named `body` is the unmarked content, and any other name is a named region.
Each slot is an object with the following members:
`name` and `label`: the slot's key and the label the insert form shows.
`kind`: `'inline'`, `'markdown'`, or `'repeatable'`.
`required`: whether the insert form requires the slot.
A required slot shows an asterisk, and **Insert** stays disabled until the slot is filled.
A touched, empty slot shows `<label> is required.`
`itemFields`: for a repeatable slot, the item's field.
The insert form reads only the first declared field's key.
Each item is one string under that key, or under `text` when `itemFields` is absent.
`itemLabel(item, index)`: for a repeatable slot, a function that names each row in the insert form.
When it returns nothing or blank text, the row reads as the slot label plus the row number.
The render never reads `required`, so a hand-typed directive without the slot still renders.
In the `event` declaration, add a `slots` array with a required inline `title`, a markdown `body`, and a repeatable `agenda` whose `itemLabel` returns the item's text:
`build` runs once for each occurrence of the directive.
It receives a context and synchronously returns one hast `Element`.
The context carries the following members:
`attributes`: the declared attribute values, keyed by name, with a `boolean` as `true` or `false`.
`slot(name)`: a slot's rendered children, or an empty array when the slot is absent.
`items(name)`: a repeatable slot's items, one child list per item.
`attr(key)`: a declared attribute's string value, or `undefined` for a boolean or absent attribute.
`node`: the stamped component element.
The context builds no markup.
A `build` makes its markup with hastscript's `h()`.
It can draw an icon with the engine's `renderGlyph`, which returns an `svg` element from the site's icon set.
Each path in that set is filled shape data.
A stroke-only path renders invisible.
In the `event` declaration, replace the `build` stub with a function that arranges the slots and attributes in one element:
`build` can't `await`.
Data a component needs is fetched outside the render and reaches `build` through `attributes`.
`build` runs in the editor's browser for the preview and on the server for the public page, so it can't depend on a server-only module.
The engine stamps `data-rise` on each top-level component's result, carrying the component's index in document order.
A `build` needs no entrance-motion code.
DaisyUI generates CSS for any of its component class names, such as `card-body`, that it finds in scanned source.
A component's inner classes need names that match none of them.
A reused name is restyled when the site enables that DaisyUI component elsewhere.
The example's `event-*` classes follow that rule.
A `build` that throws makes the whole render throw.
The [`ComponentContext`](../reference/render.md#types) entry documents the context's types.
The editor's picker lists a component that declares an attribute, a slot, or an `insertTemplate`, unless the component sets `hidden`.
The following optional members shape the component's row:
`icon`: a glyph key from the site's icon set, shown beside the label.
`group`: the heading the row sits under.
Groups appear in the order first declared, and ungrouped components lead with no heading.
`use`: one line on when to reach for the component.
`hidden`: a flag that leaves the component out of the top-level picker.
`preview`: a sample of attribute and slot values.
When the admin page passes `CairnAdmin` a `render`, declaring `preview` opens the insert form in two panes, with a live preview beside the form.
`insertTemplate`: the markdown inserted at the cursor when an author chooses a component with no attributes and no slots.
A component with either opens the insert form.
The `event` row sits under an **Events** heading, with a glyph, a use line, and a preview sample.
In the `event` declaration, add the picker members:
`defineRegistry({ components })` builds the registry.
The render pipeline reads it through `createRenderer`, and the picker reads the `registry` prop that the admin page passes to `CairnAdmin`.
On a scaffolded site, the adapter's registry, its renderer, and the admin page already read the module's `components` list, and one step registers the component:
At the end of `markdown-components.ts`, add `event` to the `components` list.
On a hand-built site, follow these steps:
In the adapter file, build the registry with `defineRegistry({ components: [event] })`.
In the same file, pass the registry as the first argument of the `createRenderer` call.
In the adapter's `rendering` group, set `components` to the registry.
In `src/routes/admin/[...path]/+page.svelte`, pass `registry={cairn.rendering.components}` to `CairnAdmin`.
The scaffold's admin page passes the registry to `CairnAdmin` beside the render function:
An admin page that passes no `registry` shows no **Insert block** button.
`defineRegistry` throws for a component named `figure` or `include`.
Its message says to remove the component if the built-in covers its use, or to rename it.
It also throws for a component that sets a non-empty `defaultIconByRole` but declares no attribute of type `icon`.
The [`defineRegistry`](../reference/core.md#defineregistry) entry documents the registry.
The insert form writes a component with named slots inside a four-colon outer fence, and each named slot becomes a nested `:::name` container.
The insert form writes the `event` directive with the title as the label, the details unmarked, and the agenda items as bullets:
`createRenderer` turns that directive into the following HTML, including the `data-rise` stamp that the engine adds to the result of `build`:
A repeatable slot's items are bullet lines inside its container.
A bracketed label is dropped when the component declares no `title` slot.
A component with no named slots takes a three-colon fence.
The engine's `:::figure` and `::include` directives are not components, and a leaf or text form of any component name stays literal.
A working component inserts from the picker, renders in the edit page's preview, and carries the same classes on the published page.
To verify the component, follow these steps:
In a terminal at the project root, start the dev server.
In the admin, open an entry.
On the **Write** tab, select **Insert block**.
In the picker, under the **Events** heading, choose **Event**.
In the insert form, fill the required fields.
In the insert form, select **Insert**.
**Insert** stays disabled while a required slot is empty.
In the editor, check that the inserted markdown matches the directive in [Component authoring grammar](#component-authoring-grammar).
In the toolbar, select the **Preview** tab.
In the preview, check that the component renders with its `event` classes.
In the admin, publish the entry.
After the site deploys, check that the component's element on the public page carries the classes the preview showed.
Each failed check traces to the component's declaration, the admin page's wiring, or the markdown an author wrote.
When a check fails, work through the following causes in order:
The site fails to load with an error that names the component.
A bad attribute type, a reserved name, and a `defaultIconByRole` without an `icon` attribute each throw that error.
So does a `hydrate` component without a matching `rendering.islands` entry, or an entry without its component.
Fix the member the error names.
The editor shows no **Insert block** button.
Either the admin page passes `CairnAdmin` no `registry`, or the registry holds no component the picker lists.
Pass the registry as [Register the component](#register-the-component) shows.
The component is missing from the picker.
It declares no attribute, no slot, and no `insertTemplate`, or it sets `hidden`.
The preview shows `The preview could not render this content.`
The render threw, for example because `build` threw on a value it didn't expect.
The directive prints as literal text.
It was written in the leaf `::name` or text `:name` form.
Rewrite it as a `:::name` container.
The component's content renders without its markup.
No component in the registry that `createRenderer` received has the directive's name.
Register the component, or correct the directive's name.
A code block shows no token colors.
Its fence names no language, or a language outside the highlighter's preloaded set, and the highlighter renders it as plain text.
A `mermaid` fence passes through untouched.
For a failure this list doesn't cover, see [Read the structured logs](debug-your-site.md#read-the-structured-logs).
